doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Demanding pay equal to male musicians in Europe
summary: She insisted on the same money and better hotels than the men, which did not please the male musicians.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you ever have opportunities open up in Europe as things dried up in the States, especially in the ‘60’s?
I don’t think so. Usually people call you in Europe when they need you. I guess that’s every club owner. I get more gigs now than…
I read somewhere that you got in trouble with some of the European bookers for demanding and commanding the salaries that the male musicians were getting paid.
I didn’t get in trouble, I just said I should make the same money if I’m playing better or as well. And staying in better hotels.
Yeah, ‘cause I wasn’t gonna stay in the dumps. They put the musicians in dumps you know.
How did the male musicians feel about you commanding the same salaries as they were getting? Were they resentful or supportive?
